current_claim: Each test is a function of O(log m) input bits, at most ell+1 for a pointer test.
recommended_statement: Each test is evaluable by a deterministic adaptive bit-query decision tree of depth O(log m). A pointer test first reads ell pointer bits and then the selected target bit, using at most ell+1 queries. Gate tests inspect at most three fixed bits.
reason: At m=4, a two-bit pointer selects one of x0,x1,x2,x3. The resulting function depends on all six variables but has decision-tree depth three. Thus query depth and number of relevant variables differ.
source: paper/quartic-query-separation.pdf, Lemma 2.2 pp.6–7; corpus/statement_ledger.json row lem-2.2.i
formal_target: Model a pointer test as an adaptive decision tree of depth ell+1; coherent evaluation follows by retaining and uncomputing pointer/index registers.
impact: Correct the ledger and its proof_notes; no correction to the manuscript lemma is indicated.
